..
An unstable weather pattern due to nearby Invest 97W will bring
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms tonight for the Marianas
with slightly higher chances for Guam. High end scattered showers 
and isolated thunderstorms are expected to continue through Thursday
as a monsoon-like pattern brings moisture and southwesterly winds 
into the area. Some uncertainty remains as to where exactly the surge
will develop over the Marianas and whether winds will be gusty or
not. This will depend on the strength and location of 97W over the
next few days. This monsoon pattern may shift out of the Marianas
late this week or over the weekend bringing dryer air and isolated
showers and thunderstorms.

Marine...
Gentle to moderate south winds will turn southwest tonight and 
likely remain southwest through Saturday. Combined seas of 5 to 6 
feet tonight consist of a building southwest swell, a diminishing
west swell, and the typical east trade-wind swell. There will be a 
moderate risk of rip currents tonight for all reefs, and then just
south and west reefs by Tuesday. The rip risk could become high 
along south and west facing reefs Wednesday as a southwest swell 
builds in. There will also be a moderate risk of lightning all this 
week as wet season builds in.The southwest swell will be monitored 
closely this week in case it reaches hazardous levels depending on 
the strength of Invest 97W and the developing monsoon surge. Isolated
thunderstorms are possible for the whole forecast period.

Tropical Systems...
The Joint Typhoon Warning Center issue a tropical formation alert
(TCFA) this afternoon for Invest 97W, meaning that the disturbance is
expected to become a tropical depression within the next 24 hours.
97W is currently located around 11N136E. Ensemble guidance suggests 
that the disturbance will drift westward over the next day or so 
before curving to the north, well west of the Marianas. Guidance then
continues that northward trend through late this week before taking 
it to the northeast. 97W very broad and asymmetrical with scattered
to widespread showers and isolated thunderstorms on all sides. The
westerly wind burst on the southern half is expected to become more
of a monsoon surge and expand towards the Marianas. Residents in
Palau, Yap, and the Marianas should continue to monitor this system
for further development and the risk of hazardous seas, increased
rainfall, and gusty winds.

Eastern Micronesia...
Satellite imagery late this afternoon shows isolated to scattered 
showers in the vicinity of all three forecast sites with these 
conditions expected to continue into Tuesday. Invest 98W was closed 
this afternoon by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center, meaning that no 
development is expected to occur with this disturbance. Though, the 
disturbance will drift generally westward over the coming days and 
bring periods of increased cloud cover and showers at Kosrae and 
Pohnpei starting Tuesday night. Shower coverage should remain 
scattered at Kosrae into latter part of the week, but potential wet 
weather may be in store for Pohnpei Wednesday and Thursday, 
especially Wednesday. Isolated thunderstorms will be possible at both
locations through the week. Isolated to low-end scattered showers 
are expected to prevail at Majuro through Friday. 

North to northeast winds will continue at Pohnpei through Tuesday 
and through tonight at Kosrae. Winds will become east to southeast as
former Invest 98W drifts south of the islands through Wednesday and 
then shift to southwest by Thursday night at both locations as the 
disturbance continues its westward trek. Winds are expected to be 
gentle to moderate with fresh winds possible, especially at Pohnpei, 
during that southwest burst. East to southeast light to gentle winds 
are expected to continue at Majuro through Tuesday before becoming 
light and southerly Wednesday. Combined seas of 4 to 5 feet will 
continue to diminish through Wednesday, becoming mostly 3 to 4 feet 
by late week. Seas consist of a west swell at Kosrae and Pohnpei and 
an east swell at Majuro. A small, south to southeast swell is also 
present throughout all waters.

Western Micronesia...
The High Surf Advisory has been extended through Sunday afternoon at
Yap, and a new Small Craft Advisory was issued for Yap and a Special
Weather Statement has been issued for Yap and Palau.

For Palau and Yap, showers are being produced by the outer reaches 
of Invest 97W. These showers are expected to remain over Koror and
Colonia. Showers over the next few days are expected to produce 0.5
to 1 inches of rain. As Invest 97W pulls away, a monsoon trough will
maintain showers through there weekend.

For Chuuk, a the Near-Equatorial Trough, a north-south facing trough
and a weak circulation near Nukuoro are nearby. Tonight, scattered
showers are expected to move in over Weno. As the north-south facing
trough and circulation moves westward, are expected to build back
into the region around Wednesday.
